drafts.after: Seventy weeks are determined upon your people and your holy city. These weeks are counted in prophetic time, not on an ordinary calendar. The transgression is finished. Sins are ended. Reconciliation is made for iniquity. Everlasting righteousness is brought in. Vision and prophecy are sealed up. The Most Holy is anointed. Textual proof: the window includes Messiah's mission (v25-27). Hebrews 9:26 speaks of Christ appearing at the end of the ages to put away sin by Himself.
drafts.reason: This is the gate failure: the 43-word opening run chained the seventy weeks, the people, the city and all six purposes through commas and never stopped, so the gate counted one long sentence. It is now sentences that each carry one idea, and the longest is 18 words. All six purposes survive word for word in the verse's own passive form, so no agent is added to them: finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, anoint the Most Holy. 'Seventy weeks are determined upon your people and your holy city', 'the window includes Messiah's mission (v25-27)' and Hebrews 9:26 are byte-identical, and no number was added, moved or changed: 70, v25-27 and Hebrews 9:26 stand as they were. 'seventy weeks' is no longer left unexplained: the second sentence says what kind of time it is, taken from this entry's own term note (Prophetic day-units), without adding a number or a date.

drafts.after: The book is sealed until the time of the end, when knowledge runs to and fro. First principle: prophecy can stay sealed and unclear for a long time. The seal opens when the world is ready to run with it.
drafts.reason: V3: 'prophecy has a shelf-life of obscurity' becomes 'prophecy can stay sealed and unclear for a long time'. V2: the dash chain is split into one idea per sentence. The seal until the time of the end and 'the seal opens when the world is ready to run with it' keep their claims. The app's clause 'knowledge runs to and fro' is left exactly as it stood; it sits outside quotation marks, so it is not modernised and no QUOTE-REVIEW is raised.

drafts.after: Gabriel will show you what has been written in the true record. Michael stands as your prince. First principle: history is written down before it happens. The scripture of truth is the record, and empires must act it out.
drafts.reason: V2: the semicolon pair is split, and the first sentence takes its object ('will show you what has been written'). V3: 'the scripture of truth is the script empires must play out' becomes 'is the record, and empires must act it out'. Gabriel, Michael, 'your prince' and the KJV phrase 'the scripture of truth' stand.

drafts.after: He shall confirm a covenant — God's binding promise — with many for one week. In the middle of the week he causes sacrifice and oblation, the temple offerings, to cease. First principle: Messiah's death ends the old system of sacrifices, and it no longer does what it was meant to do (Heb 10).
drafts.reason: V3: 'covenant' carries the frozen glossary rendering in place; 'oblation' is glossed as the temple offerings; 'in the midst' becomes 'In the middle of the week'; and 'efficacy' becomes 'it no longer does what it was meant to do'. V2: the semicolon pair is split. 'for one week', 'sacrifice and oblation', '(Heb 10)' and the claim that Messiah's death ends the old sacrificial system are unchanged.

drafts.after: Armed forces pollute the sanctuary and end the daily sacrifice. This is the desecration Jesus tells readers to watch for. First principle: Daniel 11 is Matthew 24's source text. The abomination — the thing that makes the holy place desolate — is scheduled, and flight is commanded.
drafts.reason: V3: 'Arms' becomes 'Armed forces', and the bare label 'the abomination' now says what it is (the thing that makes the holy place desolate), which the brief requires. V2: the 18-word dash-joined sentence and the semicolon pair are split. Daniel 11 and Matthew 24 are byte-identical, and every claim stands: the sanctuary polluted, the daily sacrifice ended, the desecration Jesus points readers to, the abomination scheduled, flight commanded.

drafts.after: Behind the empires you see, other princes are fighting, and Michael comes to help. First principle: prayer on earth touches a war in heaven. When an answer is delayed, that does not mean the angels are gone.
drafts.reason: V3: 'Behind the curtain of empires, princes contend' becomes a plain sentence about princes who are fighting. V2: the semicolon pair is split, and 'the delay of answers is not the absence of angels' is said in plain word order. Michael, prayer on earth, the war in heaven and the angels are unchanged.

drafts.after: Michael stands up. Trouble comes like nothing before it. Everyone written in the book is delivered. First principle: the worst time in history has a list of names. Deliverance is written down, not left to chance.
drafts.reason: V2: the 18-word semicolon chain of three events becomes three sentences, one idea each. V3: 'unparalleled trouble' becomes 'Trouble comes like nothing before it', 'register of names' becomes 'list of names', and 'not random' becomes 'not left to chance'. Michael, the book, the deliverance of everyone written in it and the worst time in history are unchanged.

drafts.after: A blessing is promised to those who endure to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. First principle: waiting is blessed when the timeline belongs to God. The waiting has a set number of days.
drafts.reason: V3: 'A beatitude attaches to' becomes 'A blessing is promised to', and 'endurance has a numbered horizon' becomes 'The waiting has a set number of days.' V2: the em-dash chain is split. The day count 'the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days' (Dan 12:12) is byte-identical and the claim that endurance is blessed is kept at full strength.

drafts.after: After sixty-two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for Himself. First principle: the Anointed One does not die for His own sin. He dies for others, and Isaiah 53 confirms it.
drafts.reason: V2: 'the Anointed One dies not for His own sin but for others — Isaiah 53 confirmed' becomes two sentences with a verb, and 'confirmed' takes its actor. 'After sixty-two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for Himself' is byte-identical, including the sixty-two weeks of Dan 9:26, and the Isaiah 53 citation is untouched.

drafts.after: Many who sleep in the dust shall awake. Some wake to everlasting life, and some to shame. Jesus and Paul and Revelation all cite a bodily resurrection. First principle: death is not the end. Everyone rises, and that rising settles everything.
drafts.reason: V2: the colon chain and the semicolon pair are split into one idea per sentence. V3: 'death is not final; resurrection is universal and decisive' becomes 'death is not the end' and 'Everyone rises, and that rising settles everything', which keeps both claims (universal, decisive) without softening either. 'Many who sleep in the dust shall awake', Jesus, Paul and Revelation are unchanged.

drafts.after: The man in linen swears an oath about how long it lasts. When the scattering of the holy people's power is complete, all is finished. First principle: he swears to the end of the persecution. It runs three-and-a-half times, and then it is over.
drafts.reason: V2: the 'oath-sworn duration' fragment becomes a sentence and the em-dash chain is split. V3: 'accomplished' becomes 'complete' and 'then done' becomes 'and then it is over'. 'the scattering of the holy people's power', 'all is finished', the man in linen and the three-and-a-half times are preserved byte for byte.

drafts.after: Daniel is told to go his way and rest. He will rise for his portion at the end of days. First principle: the faithful die with a place kept for them. They rest now, and they stand at the end.
drafts.reason: V2: 'dismissed to rest and to rise for his portion' becomes two sentences, and the em-dash chain is split. V3: 'reserved lot' becomes 'a place kept for them'. Daniel, his portion, the end of days and the claim that the faithful rest now and stand at the end are unchanged.

drafts.after: The glorious man stands by the river. His body is like beryl, his eyes are fire, his feet are like brass, and his voice is like a multitude. First principle: God appears to someone here, before the visions begin. The glory of the messenger shows how much the message weighs.
drafts.reason: V2: the colon chain is split and the compressed description takes verbs, one part per clause. V3: 'theophany' carries the frozen glossary rendering (God appears to someone), 'apocalypse' becomes 'the visions', and 'certifies the message's weight' becomes 'shows how much the message weighs'. Every part of the description (beryl, fiery eyes, brass feet, the voice of a multitude) is kept.

drafts.after: The abomination — the thing that makes the holy place desolate — is set up, and a counted span begins. First principle: God numbers the desolation. The day counts mean the horror has limits you can measure.
drafts.reason: V3: the bare label 'the abomination' now says what it is, and 'measurable, curfew-able bounds' becomes 'limits you can measure'. V2: the counted span and the dash chain are split into one idea per sentence. 'God numbers the desolation' and the counted span are unchanged.

drafts.after: Daniel counts from the decree to restore Jerusalem to the coming of Messiah the Prince. First principle: Daniel gives the coming of the Anointed One a window you can calculate.
drafts.reason: V2: the verbless fragment 'From the decree ... until Messiah the Prince' becomes a sentence with a verb and a subject. V3: 'within a calculable window' becomes 'a window you can calculate'. The decree to restore Jerusalem, Messiah the Prince and the Anointed One are unchanged.
